title: Research best-effort F_5 packed encoding
description:
## Context

⚠ **User approval required** before selecting the winning encoding — this is the input contract for W4 implementation issues T17/T18.

The bipedal F₃ encoding minimises bitwise op counts (2 ops/mul, 6 ops/add) by using a 4-state alphabet with one redundant codeword. F₅ has 5 elements; the simplest baseline is 3-bit-per-element packed (one redundant codeword in 8 states, 16 elements per `u64`) with a 2¹⁶-entry table-LUT for mul. Better encodings may exist by exploiting the multiplicative structure (F₅* is cyclic of order 4 — log/sign split is plausible).

This issue prototypes 2–4 candidate encodings in `dev/research/f5_packing/` (mirroring `dev/research/rns_prototype/`), measures cycles/op for each on synthetic workloads, and produces a decision document selecting the winning candidate.

Hard fallback if no novel encoding beats the LUT baseline by ≥ 1.5×: select the 3-bit + LUT baseline. The fallback is acceptable; document it as the chosen encoding in the decision doc.

## Success Criteria

1. [hard] `dev/research/f5_packing/` exists, builds with `cargo build -p f5-packing-prototype --release`.
2. [hard] At least 2 candidate encodings are implemented and benchmarked.
3. [hard] `dev/plans/r1_f5_encoding_decision.md` lands and is attached via `jit doc add`, naming the winning candidate with measured cycles/op.
4. [hard] Decision doc documents the bitwise op counts for add, sub, mul, div on the chosen encoding.
5. [hard] User has signed off on the chosen encoding (recorded as a comment) before transitioning to `done`.
